description:
False-colour satellite imagery showing land cover classification within a Natura 2000 (N2K) site, specifically identifying wetland areas. The image displays a central water body with surrounding land. A green line outlines the "Border of Natura 2000 site". Within this site, blue arrows point to two distinct land cover types:
1.  An area with significant vegetation cover, identified as having "Reeds > 30%", which is classified as "7.1.1 Inland marshes".
2.  A large, open expanse of water, labelled as "Open water visible in imagery", which is classified as "8.2.1 Natural lakes".
The imagery distinguishes between open water, dense reedbeds, and surrounding land features like agricultural fields (shown in reddish tones) and possibly a built-up area (lighter teal/greenish tones) on the left side. The map demonstrates a specific CLMS (Copernicus Land Monitoring Service) classification logic for wetland habitats, showing how areas with different proportions of reeds are differentiated from open water bodies, consistent with the Natura 2000 site requirements for habitat mapping. The surrounding context indicates this is likely the Tablas de Daimiel Natura 2000 Site in Central Spain.
